items.title: On World Cities Day 2026, WHO calls for safe, healthy housing for all
items.summary: This World Cities Day, celebrated under the theme “Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All”, the World Health Organization (WHO) highlights the critical role of housing in shaping health and well-being and calls for greater action to ensure that everyone can live in healthy, safe and accessible homes.

items.title: Barbados eliminates mother-to-child transmission of HIV
items.summary: Barbados has eliminated mother-to-child transmission of HIV as a public health problem, the World Health Organization (WHO) announced, marking a major public health milestone resulting from years of sustained efforts to ensure babies are born free of HIV.

items.title: World Conference on Traditional Medicine 2026 delivers landmark outcomes for global health
items.summary: Expert Committee Meeting members at the World Conference on Traditional Medicine 2026© WHOThe World Conference on Traditional Medicine 2026 concluded in Beijing on 18 October with several key outcomes aimed at strengthening global cooperation for health and well-being. items.title: Announcement of candidates for the position of WHO Director-General
items.summary: Seven candidates have been proposed by Member States of the World Health Organization for the position of WHO Director-General. The candidates will engage with Member States and Associate Members on 18–19 November 2026 at the first candidates’ forum at WHO Headquarters in Geneva.

items.title: Message by the Director of the Department of Immunization, Vaccines and Biologicals at WHO - October 2026
items.summary: From 5 to 8 October, the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE) met to review the evidence on vaccines against human papillomavirus (HPV), diphtheria, yellow fever, mpox and polio, and to consider the role of vaccination in the ongoing Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak.

items.title: WHO country leaders strengthen skills to advance tobacco control
items.summary: WHO Representatives and Heads of Country Offices from 13 countries gathered at the WHO Academy in Lyon, France, on 29–30 September 2026 for the sixth Executive Leadership Programme for Tobacco Control, strengthening the leadership skills, strategic partnerships and collaboration needed to accelerate progress against tobacco use.

items.title: Statement by WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus concerning the train accident in Spain
items.summary: We came to Madrid this week as partners in the Global Obesity Summit, to talk about health, and how we can help people everywhere live longer, fuller lives. This morning, that purpose tragically overshadowed by a terrible train accident south of this city that has taken many lives.

items.title: WHO advises coexistence of digital and non-digital ship-related health documents
items.summary: WHO calls on States Parties to facilitate the coexistence of digital and non-digital formats of ship-related health documents, including the Ship Declaration of Health (SDH) and Ship Sanitation Certificates (SSC), following the 2024 amendments to the International Health Regulations (2005) (IHR), which entered into force for most States Parties on 19 September 2025.

items.title: Climate change is a growing health emergency, Lancet Countdown warns
items.summary: Ahead of COP31, the latest Lancet Countdown report finds that the health impacts of climate change are accelerating, with heat-related deaths, drought and other climate-related risks increasing faster than a decade ago, even as clean energy investments and climate action begin to deliver health benefits.

items.title: WHO releases target regimen profiles for long-acting injectables for TB
items.summary: WHO has published Target regimen profiles for long-acting injectables (LAIs) for tuberculosis (TB) prevention and treatment, which still depend on daily oral regimens taken over months, and sustaining adherence over such periods is difficult for many people. LAIs could significantly lighten the burden for people taking TB medicines and the health system that delivers them.

items.title: Types of data requested to inform December 2026 COVID-19 vaccine antigen composition deliberations
items.summary: The WHO Technical Advisory Group on COVID-19 Vaccine Composition (TAG-CO-VAC) continues to closely monitor the genetic and antigenic evolution of SARS-CoV-2 variants, immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19 vaccination, and the performance of COVID-19 vaccines against circulating variants.

items.title: WHO launches working papers on traditional medicine
items.summary: The WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre is launching a series of working papers designed to document and examine traditional, complementary and integrative medicine (TCIM) worldwide. The inaugural publication, Cupping therapy: descriptive synthesis of training, provides a first-of-its-kind overview of training approaches for cupping therapy primarily based on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM). items.title: WHO and ENHYPEN join efforts to inspire young blood donors globally
items.summary: World Health Organization (WHO) Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus met with global K-pop group ENHYPEN in Seoul on 22 October to celebrate the success of their collaboration for World Blood Donor Day 2026 and recognize the group's role in inspiring young people around the world to donate blood and save lives.

items.title: Global Diagnostics Coalition calls for collective action to close the diagnostic gap
items.summary: The Global Diagnostics Coalition (GDC) convened leaders from government, global health, civil society, industry and partner organizations at the World Health Summit 2026 to advance collective action to close persistent gaps in access to diagnostic services.Diagnostics are fundamental to quality health care, universal health coverage, health security and pandemic preparedness. items.title: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus - Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Between 1 January and 5 October 2026, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia reported eight laboratory-confirmed cases of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) infection, including one death. Cases were detected across six locations: Al Jouf (1), Arar (1), Hafr Al-Batin (1), Riyadh (2), Tabuk (1) and Taif (2). No epidemiological links were identified between any of the cases. items.summary: On 2 October 2026, WHO became aware through media reports of the death of an employee of the Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute (APRI) of Siberia and the Far East, the Russian Federation. According to these reports, the individual died on 2 October following hospitalization for severe pneumonia on 29 September, and pneumonic plague was suspected as the cause of death, following occupational exposure in laboratory settings. items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.summary: On 5 October 2026, WHO was informed about a laboratory-confirmed imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in Kenya with travel history from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The patient travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to Kenya through Uganda. The patient was hospitalized and treated in Kenya but subsequently died on 5 October. items.summary: Since the last Disease Outbreak News was published on 11 September 2026, the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded further, with two additional health zones affected. These include Bulu health zone in a new province, Sud Ubangi, located on the north-west part of the country and Dungu health zone in Haut-Uélé province, bordering South Sudan. items.summary: Since the last Disease Outbreak News was published on 28 August 2026, the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded to one additional health zone, Kayna, in North Kivu. items.summary: Since the last Disease Outbreak News was published on 14 August 2026, the outbreak has spread from 54 to 60 health zones. items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.summary: The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is in a phase of intense transmission. It is the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in the country and expanding faster than any previous Ebola outbreak. The epidemic is increasingly characterized by sustained transmission within interconnected geographic clusters. items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.summary: The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is intensifying, with sustained transmission and continued increases in reported cases and deaths.
